candidates.text: A grammar quiz taken by nearly 670,000 people suggests native-like fluency in a new language is rarely reached unless learning starts by about age 10.
candidates.evidence: However, the study also found that it is nearly impossible for people to achieve proficiency similar to that of a native speaker unless they start learning a language by the age of 10. … The findings are based on an analysis of a grammar quiz taken by nearly 670,000 people
candidates.check: Threshold stated directly by the source: native-like proficiency requires starting 'by the age of 10'. Placed at age 10 as the last year of that window. Single study (669,498 participants, published in Cognition, May 2018). A 2022 reanalysis (Slik et al., Language Learning) disputes the sharply defined critical age reported by the original study; this candidate relies on the original study as reported by MIT News.

candidates.text: The World Health Organization counts adolescence from 10 to 19. There are more adolescents alive than ever before: 1.3 billion, one in six people on Earth.
candidates.evidence: Adolescence is the phase of life between childhood and adulthood, from ages 10 to 19. … There are more adolescents in the world than ever before: 1.3 billion, totalling one sixth of the global population.
candidates.check: WHO defines adolescence as ages 10 to 19, so age 10 is its first year. Global figure (1.3 billion, one sixth of world population) as stated on the WHO health-topic page, current as fetched in Sept 2026; the page gives no reference year.

candidates.text: Writing under the name Gul Makai, Malala Yousafzai was 11 when she began an anonymous diary for BBC Urdu about her wish to go to school.
candidates.evidence: In early 2009, Malala started to blog anonymously on the Urdu language site of the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC). She wrote about life in the Swat Valley under Taliban rule, and about her desire to go to school. … Malala was 11 years old when she wrote her first BBC diary entry.
candidates.check: Born 1997-07-12 (NobelPrize.org facts page: 'Born: 12 July 1997, Mingora, Pakistan', https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2014/yousafzai/facts/); first BBC Urdu diary entry in early 2009 (NobelPrize.org biographical), i.e. before her 12th birthday on 2009-07-12 -> 11. The Nobel page also states the age explicitly. Pen name 'Gul Makai' is on the same page.

candidates.text: The NHS gives 11 as the average age for girls to start puberty, and 12 for boys, though anywhere from 8 to 14 is normal.
candidates.evidence: The average age for girls to start puberty is 11, while for boys the average age is 12. … But it's perfectly normal for puberty to begin at any point between the ages of 8 and 13 in girls and 9 and 14 in boys.
candidates.check: NHS (Wales) health A-Z page: average onset age 11 for girls (placed at age 11), 12 for boys; normal range 8-13 in girls and 9-14 in boys, so '8 to 14' covers both. UK guidance, no survey year given.

candidates.text: Brain charts built from 123,984 MRI scans place the peak of total cerebrum volume at about twelve and a half years.
candidates.evidence: we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans … total surface area closely tracked the development of total cerebrum volume (TCV) across the lifespan (Fig. 2a ), with both metrics peaking at approximately 11–12 years of age (surface area peak at 10.97 years (95% bootstrap CI 10.42–11.51); TCV peak at 12.5 years (95% bootstrap CI 12.14–12.89).
candidates.check: Peak of total cerebrum volume (TCV) at 12.5 years (95% CI 12.14-12.89), which falls inside the age-12 window (12.0-12.99). Pooled from 123,984 scans of 101,457 people across more than 100 studies (Brain charts for the human lifespan, Nature 2022, open-access copy on PMC).

candidates.text: From about 6 to 12, the outer layers of the brain's hearing cortex mature, as children grow sharper at telling the sounds of language apart.

source.label: Moore & Linthicum, International Journal of Audiology, 2007

candidates.evidence: Later childhood, from six to twelve years, is the time of maturation of the superficial cortical layers and their intracortical connections, accompanied by appearance of the N(1) potential and improved linguistic discriminative abilities.
candidates.check: Review 'The human auditory system: a timeline of development' gives later childhood, six to twelve years, as the period when the superficial layers of the auditory cortex mature; age 12 is the end of that window. Abstract text read via the Europe PMC API mirror of PubMed (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:17828663%20AND%20SRC:MED&resultType=core&format=json) because pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov returned a captcha to automated fetches.

candidates.text: In August 1963 'Fingertips – Pt 2' made Stevie Wonder the youngest solo artist ever to reach No. 1 on the US Billboard Hot 100.
candidates.evidence: Aug. 10, 1963 Stevie Wonder … iconic debut single, “Fingertips – Pt 2,” topped the Billboard Hot 100 for the first of three weeks. The song made him the youngest soloist ever to lead the Hot 100 … He was born Stevland Hardaway Morris (he also used the surname Judkins as a boy) on May 13, 1950 in Saginaw, Michigan.
candidates.check: Born 1950-05-13 (Detroit Historical Society, https://www.detroithistorical.org/learn/online-research/encyclopedia-of-detroit/wonder-stevie); song topped the Hot 100 on 1963-08-10 (Billboard). 1963-08-10 is after his 13th birthday on 1963-05-13 -> 13 (13 years 89 days).

candidates.text: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine's range for teenagers aged 13 to 18 is 8 to 10 hours of sleep a day, down from 9 to 12 for children.

source.label: Paruthi et al., AASM consensus, J Clin Sleep Med (via PMC), 2016

candidates.evidence: Children 6 to 12 years of age should sleep 9 to 12 hours per 24 hours … Teenagers 13 to 18 years of age should sleep 8 to 10 hours per 24 hours on a regular basis to promote optimal health.
candidates.check: AASM consensus statement: the teenage band starts at 13 (8-10 h per 24 h), replacing the 6-12 band (9-12 h). Age 13 is the first year of the new band. US professional body recommendation, 2016.

candidates.text: In a study of 463 Danish choirboys, the median age at which the voice broke was 14.0 years.

source.label: Juul et al., International Journal of Andrology, 2007

candidates.evidence: retrospective analyses of age at voice break in 463 Danish choir boys … We found an overall median age at voice break of 14.0 [13.9-14.6] years
candidates.check: Median age at voice break 14.0 years (bracketed interval in the abstract: 13.9-14.6) in 463 Danish choirboys studied over 1994-2003 (Denmark). 14.0 falls in the age-14 window. Abstract read via Europe PMC API (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:17459124%20AND%20SRC:MED&resultType=core&format=json) because PubMed returned a captcha to automated fetches.

candidates.text: In March 1944, in hiding in Amsterdam, Anne Frank heard a radio appeal to keep wartime diaries, and began planning a book: The Secret Annex.
candidates.evidence: On 28 March 1944, the people in hiding in the Secret Annex heard an appeal on Radio Orange from Dutch minister Bolkestein. … Letters, for instance, or diaries, or speeches. His request inspired Anne and she planned to publish a book about her time in hiding after the war. … She also came up with a title: ‘Het Achterhuis’ or ‘The Secret Annex’. … the red-checked diary she got for her thirteenth birthday on 12 June 1942.
candidates.check: Born 1929-06-12 (Anne Frank House: diary received 'for her thirteenth birthday on 12 June 1942', https://www.annefrank.org/en/museum/collection/anne-frank-collection/35/red-checked-diary/); radio appeal heard 1944-03-28 (Anne Frank House timeline). 1944-03-28 is before her 15th birthday (1944-06-12) and after her 14th -> 14. The same page gives her chosen title, 'Het Achterhuis' ('The Secret Annex').

candidates.text: In March 1955, 15-year-old Claudette Colvin refused to give up her seat on a segregated bus in Montgomery, nine months before Rosa Parks.
candidates.evidence: She was 15-year-old Claudette Colvin, and it was March 1955, nine months before Parks … On March 2, 1955, she was arrested at the age of 15 in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give up her seat to a white woman on a crowded, segregated bus. … Born in Birmingham, Alabama, in 1939
candidates.check: Event 1955-03-02 (National Geographic; also Equal Justice Initiative, https://eji.org/news/eji-remembers-civil-rights-pioneer-claudette-colvin/: 'On March 2, 1955, 15-year-old Claudette Colvin...'). Birth year 1939 (National Geographic); exact birth date (widely given as 1939-09-05) was not confirmed on a fetched page, but both sources state her age as 15 on the day -> 15.

candidates.text: The United Nations counts ages 15 to 24 as youth. About 1.2 billion people fall in that span today, 16 per cent of the world's population.
candidates.evidence: defines ‘youth’ as those persons between the ages of 15 and 24 years. … Today, there are 1.2 billion young people aged 15 to 24 years, accounting for 16 per cent of the global population.
candidates.check: UN statistical definition of youth is 15-24 (General Assembly resolution 36/28, 1981), so 15 is its first year. Global count 1.2 billion (16%) as stated on the UN Youth page, fetched Sept 2026; no reference year given on the page.

candidates.text: In 2007 Austria became the first country in Europe to lower the voting age to 16 for all citizens, from 18.
candidates.evidence: Austria was the first country in Europe to lower the voting age to 16 for all citizens. … With the 2007 electoral reform, the voting age in Austria was lowered to 16 (from 18 previously).
candidates.check: Voting age 16 in Austria since the 2007 electoral reform (Federal Law Gazette I No. 28/2007), per the Austrian Parliament's own FAQ, current as fetched Sept 2026.

candidates.text: Mae Jemison graduated from high school at 16 and went on to Stanford; in 1992 she became the first African American woman in space.

source.label: NASA, Former Astronaut Mae C. Jemison

candidates.evidence: Jemison graduated high school at the age of 16 with a four-year National Achievement Scholarship. At Stanford University, she earned a BS in chemical engineering … became the first African American woman in space. … Born Oct. 17, 1956, in Decatur, Alabama
candidates.check: Born 1956-10-17 (Astronomy magazine, https://www.astronomy.com/today-in-the-history-of-astronomy/oct-17-1956-birth-of-mae-jemison/); NASA states she graduated from high school 'at the age of 16' (1973, before her 17th birthday on 1973-10-17) -> 16. Spaceflight STS-47, September 1992 (same NASA page).

candidates.text: In November 1934, 17-year-old Ella Fitzgerald went on stage at Harlem's Apollo Theater meaning to dance, sang instead, and won first prize.

source.label: US Copyright Office, Copyright Notices, Nov 2009

candidates.evidence: The 17-year-old showed up at the Harlem, New York, theater on November 21, 1934, prepared to dance, her passion at the time. … So she sang instead, bringing down the house and winning the $25 first prize. … Fitzgerald was born on April 25, 1917
candidates.check: Born 1917-04-25 and Apollo amateur night on 1934-11-21, both in the same US Copyright Office article (PDF, text extracted locally). 1934-11-21 is after her 17th birthday (1934-04-25) -> 17; the article also calls her 'The 17-year-old'.

candidates.text: Asked for their most meaningful songs, 1,891 people from around the world most often named ones released when they were about 17.
candidates.evidence: Using responses collected from 1891 participants across diverse geographical backgrounds, we analysed the release years of personally meaningful songs. Results showed an inverted U-shaped distribution peaking at age 17
candidates.check: Release years of personally meaningful songs, relative to each participant's age, form an inverted U peaking at age 17 (1,891 participants, diverse countries). Abstract read via Europe PMC API (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:40952922%20AND%20SRC:MED&resultType=core&format=json) because PubMed returned a captcha to automated fetches.

candidates.text: In April 2022 Japan lowered its age of adulthood from 20 to 18, the first change in roughly 140 years.
candidates.evidence: a law was enacted to revise a part of the Civil Code by reducing the age of majority in the Civil Code from 20 to 18 years old. … The first review of the age of majority in the approximately 140 years since the proclamation in 1876 … This revision will be effective from April 1, 2022.
candidates.check: Japanese Civil Code age of majority lowered from 20 to 18, law enacted 2018-06-13, in force 2022-04-01 (Ministry of Justice English page). Age 18 is the new threshold. Still in force as of the fetch (Sept 2026); alcohol/smoking ages stay at 20, not mentioned in text.

candidates.text: Agnes Bojaxhiu, later Mother Teresa, left her home in Skopje at 18 to join the Sisters of Loreto, an Irish order of nuns with missions in India.
candidates.evidence: was born Agnes Gonxha Bojaxhiu in Uskup, Ottoman Empire (now Skopje, North Macedonia), on August 26, 1910. … At the age of eighteen she left her parental home in Skopje and joined the Sisters of Loreto, an Irish community of nuns with missions in India.
candidates.check: Born 1910-08-26 (NobelPrize.org); the same page states she left home 'at the age of eighteen' (1928) -> 18. The page does not give the day of departure, so the age rests on the Nobel Foundation's explicit statement.

candidates.text: The mind's raw speed at processing information peaks around 18 or 19, while vocabulary goes on growing until the late 60s or early 70s.
candidates.evidence: raw speed in processing information appears to peak around age 18 or 19, then immediately starts to decline. … the new data showed a later peak, in the late 60s or early 70s.
candidates.check: Peak 'around age 18 or 19' from nearly 50,000 online participants plus standardized test norms; placed at 19, the later of the two stated years. Vocabulary peak late 60s/early 70s from the same article.

candidates.text: In 2019, average heights of 19-year-olds differed by about 20 cm between the tallest and shortest nations, with the Netherlands among the tallest.
candidates.evidence: There was a 20cm difference between 19-year-olds in the tallest and shortest nations … the nations with the tallest 19-year-olds in 2019 were in northwest and central Europe, and included the Netherlands, Montenegro, Denmark and Iceland.
candidates.check: Figures are for 19-year-olds in 2019, 193 countries (NCD Risk Factor Collaboration, The Lancet, Nov 2020), as reported by Imperial College London, which led the study.

candidates.text: An average 20-year-old native speaker of American English knows about 42,000 dictionary words, and goes on learning roughly one more every two days.

source.label: Brysbaert et al., Frontiers in Psychology, 2016

candidates.evidence: we estimate that an average 20-year-old native speaker of American English knows 42,000 lemmas … Between the ages of 20 and 60, the average person learns 6,000 extra lemmas or about one new lemma every 2 days.
candidates.check: Estimate for age 20 (median 20-year-old: 42,000 lemmas, i.e. dictionary headwords), US English speakers, crowdsourced vocabulary test. 'One every two days' refers to ages 20-60.

candidates.text: Sleep times drift later through the teens and reach their latest at around 20, a turning point proposed as a marker for the end of adolescence.

source.label: Nature News & Views on Roenneberg et al. (Current Biology), 2005

candidates.evidence: Children are typically early risers but start to sleep progressively later as they enter adolescence. They reach maximum lateness at around the age of 20, when the curve abruptly starts to decline. … the authors suggest, it is the point at which an individual's curve inverses that marks the end of adolescence.
candidates.check: Survey of 25,000 people aged 10-90 (Roenneberg et al., Curr. Biol. 2004), summarized in Nature 433:27 (2005): maximum lateness of sleep timing 'at around the age of 20'. The original paper is paywalled (cell.com returned 403), so the Nature summary is cited.

candidates.text: In 2025, young people in Finland left their parents' home at 21.4 years on average, the earliest in the EU, where the average was 26.3.
candidates.evidence: In 2025, young people in the EU left their parents’ home at an average age of 26.3 years … the lowest average ages were registered in Finland (21.4 years)
candidates.check: Eurostat news item of 2026-09-15, dataset yth_demo_030, reference year 2025: Finland 21.4 (lowest in EU), EU average 26.3. 21.4 falls in the age-21 window.

candidates.text: Until the Family Law Reform Act 1969, people in England and Wales came of full legal age at 21; the Act lowered it to 18.

source.label: legislation.gov.uk, Family Law Reform Act 1969, s.1

candidates.evidence: Reduction of age of majority from 21 to 18. … a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of eighteen instead of on attaining the age of twenty-one
candidates.check: Section 1 of the Family Law Reform Act 1969 (England and Wales), official UK legislation site: age of majority reduced from 21 to 18. Age 21 was the former threshold.

candidates.text: The ability to remember new names peaks at around 22, while memory for faces keeps improving until about 30.
candidates.evidence: Recent evidence shows that whereas short-term memory for names and inverted faces peaks around 22, neither short-term memory for faces nor quantity discrimination peaks until around 30
candidates.check: Peak 'around 22' for short-term memory for names; faces around 30. Stated in Hartshorne & Germine 2015, citing Germine, Duchaine & Nakayama 2011 (large online samples, mostly US).

candidates.text: In January 2021, Amanda Gorman read 'The Hill We Climb' at a US presidential inauguration, the youngest inaugural poet in the country's history.
candidates.evidence: Jan 20, 2021 12:20 PM EDT Amanda Gorman, at 22, is the youngest inaugural poet in U.S. history … Poet and activist Amanda S. C. Gorman was born on March 7, 1998, in Los Angeles, California.
candidates.check: Born 1998-03-07 (BlackPast.org, https://blackpast.org/african-american-history/amanda-s-c-gorman-1998/); inauguration reading 2021-01-20 (PBS NewsHour, which also gives her age as 22). 2021-01-20 is before her 23rd birthday (2021-03-07) and after her 22nd -> 22.

candidates.text: In June 1925 Werner Heisenberg went to the island of Helgoland to ease his hay fever, and there set out the first mathematical framework of quantum mechanics.
candidates.evidence: On June 6, a swollen-faced, stuffy-nosed Werner Heisenberg, then 23 years old and suffering from hay fever, left his home in central Germany for the fresh air of the North Sea island of Helgoland, hoping for relief. There, he had a breakthrough, becoming the first to articulate a mathematical framework of quantum mechanics … Born: 5 December 1901, Würzburg, Germany
candidates.check: Born 1901-12-05 (NobelPrize.org facts, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1932/heisenberg/facts/); left for Helgoland on 1925-06-06 and worked there in June 1925 (APS, which also says 'then 23 years old'). June 1925 is before his 24th birthday (1925-12-05) -> 23. APS notes historians doubt some romanticized details (the sunrise), not the trip or the work.

candidates.text: In a study of nearly 50,000 people, short-term memory kept improving until around 25 before levelling off.
candidates.evidence: The researchers gathered data from nearly 50,000 subjects … short-term memory continues to improve until around age 25, when it levels off
candidates.check: Ongoing process at 23: short-term memory still rising, levelling off around 25 (nearly 50,000 online participants). Same study as the age-19 candidate; different finding.

candidates.text: On 28 November 1967, PhD student Jocelyn Bell, 24, recorded radio pulses one and a third seconds apart: the discovery of pulsars.

source.label: University of Cambridge, Journeys of discovery

candidates.evidence: 24-year old PhD student Jocelyn Bell … on 28 November 1967, it came again, a string of pulses one-and-a third seconds apart. … Born July 15, 1943, Jocelyn Bell Burnell
candidates.check: Born 1943-07-15 (Astronomy magazine, https://www.astronomy.com/today-in-the-history-of-astronomy/july-15-1943-birth-of-jocelyn-bell-burnell/); first observation of the pulses on 1967-11-28 (University of Cambridge; the signal was first recorded, unrecognized, on 1967-08-06). Both dates fall after her 24th birthday (1967-07-15) -> 24; Cambridge also calls her a 24-year-old.

candidates.text: The prefrontal cortex, behind the forehead, is one of the last parts of the brain to mature; the brain finishes developing in the mid-to-late 20s.

source.label: National Institute of Mental Health (NIH), The Teen Brain

candidates.evidence: The brain finishes developing and maturing in the mid-to-late 20s. The part of the brain behind the forehead, called the prefrontal cortex, is one of the last parts to mature.
candidates.check: NIMH: brain maturation completes in the mid-to-late 20s, prefrontal cortex among the last regions. Placed at 24 as an ongoing process (still maturing); no single-age claim is made.
